mth.lead: Results are reconstructed from GTFS-RT data, not measured directly. Below: the rules, the limitations and how to read the map.
mth.s1.d: Vehicle position records (GTFS-RT) and timetables (GTFS) from public transport operators.
mth.s2.t: How we reconstruct a section run
mth.s2.d: We match vehicle records to the sections between stops and derive the run time of every trip.
mth.s3.t: Where the speed classes come from
mth.s3.d: Six classes, thresholds in km/h: {list}. These are starting values, to be calibrated on the data distribution.
mth.s4.d: When the sample for a section, an hour or a city is below the threshold (XX). Then we give no number and do not count it as zero.
mn.h: The result is reconstructed, not measured directly.
mn.p: We compute speed from vehicle position records (GTFS-RT) on the sections between stops. Scheduled speed comes from the timetable. The difference is a measure, not a diagnosis.
mn.i1.d: The run time of a section from vehicle records.
mn.i2.d: Records have gaps. Hours with a sample below the threshold (XX) are shown as “not enough data”.
mn.i3.d: Fleet coverage can be incomplete. A city with incomplete coverage gets a “limited” badge.
mn.short.b: comes from the timetable. Hatching: not enough data.
scr.s1.p: Every section between stops has the colour of its measured speed class.
scr.s2.h: Slow sections stand out at once.
scr.s2.p: Only classes 1 and 2 remain. The rest of the network dims, it does not disappear.
scr.s3.h: No data is a result too.
scr.s3.p: Sections without data are drawn with a dashed line and named in the legend.
scr.map.aria: Network schematic: sections in speed-class colours. Placeholder data.

qual.lead: The quality state says how much you may conclude from a city’s result. The method will set the sample and coverage thresholds.

qual.limited: There is a result, but the sample or coverage is incomplete.
qual.out: Not enough data to compare with other cities.
qual.table.caption: Data quality by city, placeholder data
